По сравнению с предыдущими двумя играми становится всё лучше, однако именно эта игра для меня выглядит как проба пера.

Почему? Вторая часть, которой нет десяток лет, переход от мужского центрального персонажа к женскому и выборы, которых стало гораздо больше... Но часть из которых стала просто бессмысленна. Выбор без выбора. 

Некая женщина подходит к тебе с просьбой помочь найти питомца и уходит. У тебя есть выбор искать его или уйти самому. Ты выбираешь искать и находишь, отдавая ей. Ты выбираешь уйти и тоже находишь, отдавая ей. Диалог при этом не меняется. 

Или ещё. За кем ты хочешь подглядывать? Одним персонажем, или другим? Ты выбираешь первого и подглядываешь за ним, а потом и за вторым. Ты выбираешь второго, подглядываешь только за вторым и видишь ту же самую сцену, что и в первом варианте. И таких странноватых выборов тут достаточно.

В целом, для меня эта игра выглядит лучше предыдущих даже учитывая это, хоть и жаль, что это только проба пера

Sakura Fantasy is still 100% Sakura DNA: cute anime girls, fanservice, hot scenes teased more than shown, and light route choices. But compared to some other entries, it feels a bit more “proper fantasy adventure” on top of the horny packaging.

The big difference here is tone and pacing: you get a more classic fantasy setting, a small party/team vibe, and more dialogue. It’s not suddenly deep writing or a real RPG, but you can tell they put a little more effort into the narrative flow. That’s why the story lands slightly better than the usual “thin excuse to chain CGs”.

Content-wise, expect the usual menu: suggestive scenes, bath/hot spring vibes, tentacle-ish fanservice, and that “cute-but-lewd” atmosphere. It stays on the same level of eroticism: soft and playful, more “anime tease” than explicit porn.

As always with Sakura: don’t pay full price. These games make sense when you grab them in a big Sakura bundle with a heavy discount.

“Sakura Fantasy” is a visual novel set in a simple magic world. Reading is the core activity. The protagonist trains as a knight and meets several powerful women who shape the journey.

The plot moves through short adventure segments. Minor battles and political hints appear, but conflicts resolve quickly. Dialogue drives all progression. Narrative depth is shallow, yet pacing stays steady.

Art is bright with expressive character portraits. Backgrounds include castles, forests, and training halls. Asset reuse is noticeable, but the presentation stays clean enough for the genre.

Music loops quietly under every scene. Tracks support relaxed reading and light action moments. Sound effects are rare. Audio direction remains minimal.

Gameplay offers dialogue choices that shift relationships and unlock small route variations. Branching is limited. The interface is simple, making navigation easy for new players.

Tone stays flirtatious with mild humor. Drama is limited. Sessions are short and easy to pause.

Overall, “Sakura Fantasy” fits players who want a low-stakes magical adventure in visual novel form. It provides predictable pacing, familiar art, and soft romance without demanding attention.

[h1]Reseña del Videojuego: Sakura Fantasy Chapter 1[/h1]

[h2]Resumen[/h2]
¿Te gustan las aventuras de fantasía con un toque picante de chicas con escasa ropa? ¡Pues, enhorabuena! Sakura Fantasy Chapter 1 te lleva a un mundo donde podrás explorar tus fantasías... literales y figurativas. Asuma el papel de una aspirante a caballera en un reino sacado directamente de un sueño de adolescence apasionado por el anime.

[h2]Aspectos Importantes e Interesantes[/h2]
Visualmente, este juego es un festín, con un arte que grita \¡anime de alta dosis cultural!\ desde cualquier ángulo. La historia... bueno, digamos que te mantendrá interesado, aunque a veces sientas que estás leyendo un fanfic elaborado por un panel de otakus enamorados. Los personajes están tan bien dibujados que podrías querer imprimir y colgar en tu pared alguna que otra escena, de no ser por el hecho que probablemente tendrías que explicarla después a tus visitas.

Para los amantes del género visual novel, hay decisiones a tomar que alterarán ligeramente tu camino, ofreciendo algo de rejugabilidad si decides que quieres explorar todas las \opciones\.

[h2]Aspectos por Mejorar[/h2]
El juego a veces podría ser más dinámico. Los segmentos de interacción limitada parece que te gritan \¡vamos, haz click y sigue adelante con la historia!\. Además, si fuese por profundidad narrativa, digamos que no vamos a mandar a Sakura Fantasy a competir con Tolstoy. Podría emplearse más desarrollo en los diálogos para dar profundidad a los personajes más allá de sus evidentes atributos físicos.

Sakura Fantasy is probably one of the best VNs from the Winged Cloud's catalogue. A short fantasy story with some pleasant yuri elements.

The story, unlike most form this developer, is actually pretty decent. It creates an interesting setting and nicely written characters. Nothing extraordinaire or surprising but still decently built. Unfortunately, this is only the first part of a longer story that will most likely never conclude. From what I've heard low sales discouraged continuation. Oh, well... Still, not a complete waste of time so it might still be worth reading if you accept lack of ending.
There are numerous choices but they have little to no effect on the story. No branching paths just brief detours.

Other than story, art is probably what sells this VN. It was done by Wanaca, and done well. The quality is higher than most western VNs, both characters and CGs. Backgrounds are detailed and pretty. The 'shiny skin' effect might be the only 'defect' if you don't like such effects (nitpicking here). Well done. Number of sprites is very limited though. Wish there was more CGs as the present ones don't always match what is happening.

Music is somewhat above average. It sure fits the events and overall theme. Would listen during work or relaxing activities.

No bugs encountered.

Overall, a decently written VN with great art (my taste) and decent music. It is not a complete story though, so I'm forced to deduct some points. 6/10
